ctor.rationale: `base(0, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.Self)` (PrimalForce.cs:15-18) == cost 0 / SKILL / RARE / SELF. No keywords, no CanonicalVars -- the Giant Rock's numbers live on card/giant_rock.

OnPlay.issue: The candidate set, the per-card upgrade and the index-preserving replacement are all faithful. C# selects `Hand.Cards.Where(c => c != null && c.IsTransformable && c.Type == CardType.Attack)` (PrimalForce.cs:23) and the sim's `if card.card_type != CardType.ATTACK: continue` is equivalent -- the missing `IsTransformable` test cannot differ here, because `IsTransformable` is `IsRemovable || Pile.Type != PileType.Deck` (CardModel.cs:739-750) and every candidate is in HAND, a combat pile, so it is unconditionally true. The upgrade branch matches (`if (IsUpgraded) CardCmd.Upgrade(cardModel)` before the transform, 27-30, == `if self.upgrade_level > 0: rock.upgrade()`), and both replace at the ORIGINAL pile index rather than appending (C# sorts transformations by pile index, CardCmd.cs:353-360; the sim writes `player.hand[idx] = rock`). THE TRANSFORM VERB IS BYPASSED: C# calls `CardCmd.Transform(item, cardModel)` (PrimalForce.cs:31), which runs the transform pipeline -- `AfterTransformedFrom` / `AfterTransformedTo` (CardModel.cs:1625-1632), the pile-add hooks, and the enchantment/affliction carry-over -- while the sim swaps the list slot and then fires only `hooks.register(rock)` and `on_card_entered_combat(rock)` (primal_force.py:40-41). So a transformed Attack's enchantment is silently destroyed and no transform hook fires. DORMANT: no ported card overrides `AfterTransformedFrom`/`To`, and the sim has no `after_transformed` listener category at all, so nothing observable is dropped until one is ported -- but note this is the IN-COMBAT sibling of creature_card_cmds gap G3 (deck transforms bypass the deck-entry hooks), which is LIVE for the deck case via the egg relics; this card is the in-combat case and the egg relics do not watch combat piles. Live the moment an enchantment or a transform hook is expected to survive an in-combat transform. Presentation, folded in: TriggerAnim (22) and the GiantRock hover tip (13), which is shown upgraded when this card is. REGRESSION TEST (sibling half only): `test/test_hook_order.py:345-365` -- `test_deck_transform_runs_modify_card_being_added_to_deck`, the strict xfail pinning seam G3's DECK case with Frozen Egg. The IN-COMBAT case this record covers has no pin, which is why it is recorded here rather than deferred to the seam.

OnUpgrade.rationale: PrimalForce.cs declares NO OnUpgrade override -- the upgrade changes no printed number, it only makes the created Giant Rocks upgraded, read from `IsUpgraded` inside OnPlay. The sim mirrors that exactly, including having no `_on_upgrade`. Same shape as card/armaments and card/cascade.

guards.what: the sim iterates `enumerate(player.hand)` and writes into the list it is iterating (primal_force.py:33-39)
guards.rationale: Safe because the replacement is an in-place index assignment rather than an insert or a remove, so the list length never changes; C# iterates a materialised `ToList()` for the same reason (PrimalForce.cs:23).
